subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: May synchronous exec-approval reads intentionally use the previous committed policy while a same-process async policy write holds the sidecar lock, or must every authorization read wait for that write to commit?
rationale: Atomic replacement prevents torn JSON but does not determine the authorization-ordering contract; stale policy during revocation or tightening is a security product choice.

options.title: Preserve write ordering
options.body: Coordinate synchronous and asynchronous access through one process-local mechanism so authorization reads wait for the in-flight policy write without self-deadlocking.

options.title: Allow committed-state reads
options.body: Accept reading the previous committed snapshot during same-process writes and document and prove that bounded stale-policy behavior is intentional.

options.title: Pause this patch
options.body: Keep fail-closed behavior until a narrower coordination design and live concurrency proof are available.

recommendation.title: Preserve write ordering
recommendation.body: Coordinate synchronous and asynchronous access through one process-local mechanism so authorization reads wait for the in-flight policy write without self-deadlocking.
